options.text: The average rate of change of the temperature over the first 6 minutes is -2 degrees Fahrenheit per minute.

options.text: The temperature is decreasing at a rate of 2 degrees Fahrenheit per minute at time $$t = 6$$ minutes.

questions.explanation: $$T'(6)$$ is the instantaneous rate of change of $$T$$ at time $$t = 6$$ minutes. Its sign (negative) says the temperature is decreasing, and its units are degrees Fahrenheit per minute.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{6x^{3} + 5}{5x^{2} + 8}$$?

options.why: This is the ratio of the constant terms, which only matters as x approaches 0.
Correct. The numerator has the higher degree and positive leading coefficients, so the outputs grow without bound.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to 3} \frac{x^{2} - 8x + 15}{x - 3}$$?

options.why: Substituting gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, an indeterminate form, not the value 0.

The expression is undefined at the point, but its outputs nearby approach a single number, so the limit exists.
Correct. The numerator factors as $$(x - 3)(x - 5)$$. Cancel $$x - 3$$ and substitute: $$3 - (5) = -2$$.

questions.explanation: Direct substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, so factor: $$x^{2} - 8x + 15 = (x - 3)(x - 5)$$. For $$x \neq 3$$ the expression equals $$x - 5$$, so the limit is $$3 - (5) = -2$$.

questions.stem: A 5-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 2 feet per second. How fast is the top of the ladder moving, in feet per second, when the bottom is 3 feet from the wall?

options.why: Correct. $$x^2 + y^2 = 25$$ gives $$x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$$. With $$x = 3$$, $$y = 4$$, $$\frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{3(2)}{4}$$.
The top slides down, so its rate is negative.
The two ends do not move at the same speed; their rates depend on the position.

questions.explanation: Let $$x$$ be the distance from the wall and $$y$$ the height. $$2x x' + 2y y' = 0$$, so $$y' = -\frac{x x'}{y} = -\frac{3 \cdot 2}{4} = -\frac{3}{2}$$ feet per second (the top is moving down).

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2} - 2 & x \leq 2 \\ 6x - 10 & x > 2 \end{cases}$$. Which of the following is true?

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} kx + 4 & x < 3 \\ x^{2} - 2 & x \geq 3 \end{cases}$$ where $$k$$ is a constant. For what value of $$k$$ is $$f$$ continuous at $$x = 3$$?

questions.explanation: $$f$$ is continuous at $$3$$ when the left-hand limit equals $$f(3) = 7$$. The left-hand limit is $$3k + 4$$, so $$3k + 4 = 7$$ and $$k = 1$$.

questions.stem: A farmer has 192 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular field along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river. What is the largest possible area of the field, in square meters?

options.why: Correct. With width $$x$$ perpendicular to the river, $$A = x(192 - 2x)$$, maximized at $$x = 48$$.
This makes all three fenced sides equal, which is not optimal.
This fences all four sides (a square), but the river side needs no fence.
This doesn't account for the two equal sides perpendicular to the river.

questions.explanation: $$A(x) = x(192 - 2x)$$, $$A'(x) = 192 - 4x = 0$$ at $$x = 48$$, and $$A'' = -4 < 0$$, so this is a maximum. The dimensions are $$48$$ by $$96$$, with area $$4608$$.

questions.stem: Consider the curve $$x^2 - xy + y^2 = 12$$, for which $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y - 2x}{2y - x}$$. At which points on the curve is the tangent line horizontal?
